title: Completed lisse sheaves and normalized finite etale systems
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite with valuation ring $A$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $X$ be a Noetherian separated scheme on which $\ell$ is invertible. On $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_X$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and $E_X=B_X[1/\varpi]$. A lisse $B_X$-module (respectively $E_X$-module) means a sheaf of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] pro-etale locally finite free over that coefficient sheaf, allowing rank zero and varying finite local ranks.

Reduction $N\mapsto(N/\varpi^nN)_{n\geq1}$ is an equivalence from lisse $B_X$-modules to the category of normalized inverse systems of finite locally free $A/\varpi^n$-module sheaves on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], with locally constant finite rank: transition maps induce $N_{n+1}\otimes_{A/\varpi^{n+1}}A/\varpi^n\cong N_n$. The inverse is $\varprojlim_n\nu_X^*N_n$, where $\nu_X^*$ is the etale-to-pro-etale inverse image [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. The functor from the raw $A$-linear localization of this lisse integral category to lisse $E_X$-modules, $N\mapsto N[1/\varpi]$, is fully faithful.

The reduction and inverse-limit equivalences, and this fully faithful rational realization, commute with module pullback on lisse objects and with finite coefficient extension. Their comparisons are the ones induced by the finite-level module pullbacks and scalar-extension maps, and satisfy the identity and composition equations.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1) and (4), with Corollary 5.1.5 for classical finite local systems; the comparison maps are reduction, inverse limit and localization. Their pullback and coefficient-extension compatibilities use these same maps. Etale-local existence of lattices is cited separately as an existing DAG node.

proof.text: Write $A_n=A/\varpi^nA$, write $(A_n)_X$ for the constant sheaf of this finite ring, and write $A_X$ for the continuous-function coefficient sheaf. The coefficient datum defining $B_X$ applies: $A$ is a Noetherian DVR, $A/\varpi$ is a finite field and hence torsion, and each $A_n$ is finite with the two-term free resolution $A\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}A$. Its levels are the sheafified presheaves $U\mapsto\operatorname{Cont}(\pi_0(|U|),A_n)$, not by definition the constant sheaves; by the final clause of [lem-weil-pbc-completed-constant-sheaf-reduction] (with $I=\varpi A$, every $A/I^n$ finite) the constant sheaf $(A_n)_X$ is that level sheaf, compatibly with the reduction maps, so $\varprojlim_n(A_n)_X=B_X$. By [lem-sfb-integral-lisse-reduction-equivalence], its canonical coefficient maps give $A_X\cong\varprojlim_n(A_n)_X=B_X$ and $B_X/\varpi^nB_X\cong(A_n)_X$. The same node identifies $A_X[1/\ell]$ with the continuous-function $E_X$. These localizations agree with the $E_X$ in the statement: the DVR conventions of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] give $\ell=u\varpi^e$ for a unit $u\in A$ and an integer $e>0$, so inverting either element inverts the other. All these identifications preserve the coefficient inclusions and residue projections. Thus the existing integral reduction equivalence applies to precisely the completed coefficient sheaf in this item, rather than to the constant sheaf with value $A$.

For each $n$, apply [det-pe-finite-local-systems-twist] with the finite discrete ring $A_n$. It gives a fully faithful equivalence between etale and pro-etale local systems with finite module models. This restricts to finite locally free objects. Indeed, if a descended etale sheaf has constant model $P$ on a nonempty etale trivializing object, intersect its pullback with a finite-free pro-etale trivializing covering. On a nonempty member of this covering its constant model is both $P$ and $A_n^r$. Taking a geometric stalk and using [lem-weil-proetale-constant-sheaf-stalk] gives $P\cong A_n^r$. Empty covering members impose no condition. Conversely an etale finite-free trivialization remains one on the pro-etale site. Hence at each finite level the two locally free categories are equivalent, with quasi-inverse $\nu_{X,*}$ as specified in the cited equivalence.

source.place: Tag 099Y, label lemma-compare-locally-constant; compare Bhatt–Scholze Corollary 5.1.5, p.35

proof.text: This finite-level comparison also identifies normalized towers, not just their individual objects. Inverse image preserves colimits and tensor products by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]; tensor over a ring is the coequalizer imposing its balancing relations, so it preserves scalar extension along $A_{n+1}\to A_n$. Explicitly, the comparison sends the inverse image of $a\otimes x$ to the corresponding tensor of the inverse-image sections. Thus a normalization isomorphism pulls back to the normalization isomorphism. Conversely use [det-pe-finite-local-systems-twist] to descend every finite-level object. A transition map is descended uniquely by full faithfulness for the ring $A_{n+1}$: its target, originally an $A_n$-module, is regarded as an $A_{n+1}$-module and is still a finite local system. The descended normalization becomes an isomorphism after $\nu_X^*$, hence is an isomorphism since an equivalence reflects inverses. Uniqueness also descends all transition and morphism equations. Consequently finite-level comparison gives an equivalence of the two normalized tower categories.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1) together with Corollary 5.1.5: passage to the normalized inverse-system categories

proof.text: Compose the tower equivalence of step 3 with [lem-sfb-integral-lisse-reduction-equivalence]. The latter has quasi-inverse the actual sheaf limit and canonical isomorphisms $N\cong\varprojlim_nN/\varpi^nN$ and $(\varprojlim_nF_n)/\varpi^n\cong F_n$. It therefore gives exactly the inverse $\varprojlim_n\nu_X^*N_n$ asserted here. The limit and its action are sectionwise by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](2); its $n$-th projection is the map inducing the displayed counit. The resulting unit and counit are natural because their composites with each projection are the residue map and the given tower map, respectively. Normalization forces all finite-level ranks to agree locally: reduction to $A/\varpi$ makes the free ranks equal, since the finite residue field has cardinality $q>1$ and $q^r=q^s$ implies $r=s$. The reconstruction node allows arbitrary varying finite local ranks, including rank zero, so no global constant-rank or positive-rank assumption has been introduced.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1), p.59: canonical unit, counit and inverse-limit functor

proof.text: For integral lisse modules $M,N$, form $H=\mathcal Hom_{B_X}(M,N)$ using [def-pur-sheaf-hom], so $H(X)=\operatorname{Hom}_{B_X}(M,N)$. Let $H[1/\varpi]$ denote the sheaf colimit of $H\xrightarrow{\varpi}H\xrightarrow{\varpi}\cdots$, whose existence and sheafified sectionwise description are [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful](2). There is a canonical map to $\mathcal Hom_{E_X}(M[1/\varpi],N[1/\varpi])$, sending a map in stage $k$ to $\varpi^{-k}$ times its scalar extension. It is an isomorphism: on a common trivializing covering for $M=B_X^r$ and $N=B_X^s$, it is the coordinate map from the localization of the finite matrix module $B_X^{sr}$ to $E_X^{sr}$, with inverse obtained by writing its finitely many entries as local fractions and taking a common exponent. The maps agree on overlaps because they are the specified scalar-extension map. This also treats $r=0$ or $s=0$.

A Noetherian underlying space is quasi-compact, and every open subspace is quasi-compact; in particular intersections of affine opens are quasi-compact. Thus $X$ satisfies the qcqs hypothesis of [det-pe-bounded-continuity-sections]. Apply it with $\mathcal R=B_X$, $U=X$, $I=\mathbf N$, and the diagram of degree-zero complexes $H\xrightarrow{\varpi}H\to\cdots$; the uniform lower bound is $a=0$ and take $q=0$. Together with step 5 it gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{B_X}(M,N)[1/\varpi]\cong H[1/\varpi](X)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{E_X}(M[1/\varpi],N[1/\varpi]).$$
Here the first term is the module localization, equivalently $E\otimes_A\operatorname{Hom}_{B_X}(M,N)$. The map sends $\varpi^{-k}f$ to $\varpi^{-k}(1\otimes f)$, so it is precisely the Hom map from the raw rational category of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves](2), restricted to the finite-free towers in step 4. It respects identity and composition because scalar multiplication does. This proves full faithfulness; it requires no assertion that every rational lisse sheaf has a global integral lattice.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(4), p.59: sections of the localized internal Hom on a qcqs scheme

proof.text:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism between schemes satisfying the statement's hypotheses. Use the underlying sheaf inverse image $f^{-1}$ of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Form $f^*N=B_Y\otimes_{f^{-1}B_X}f^{-1}N$ with the sheaf tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] and the coefficient map $f^{-1}B_X\to B_Y$ induced by the residue projections. The action on $f^{-1}N$ is the inverse image of the action on $N$, using finite-product preservation. The inverse-image tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor] identifies
$$(f^*N)/\varpi^n\cong f_n^*(N/\varpi^nN).$$
On a pure tensor it sends the class of $b\otimes x$ to $\bar b\otimes\bar x$; the inverse sends $\bar b\otimes\bar x$ to that class, with lift independence following from the quotient relation. By [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], the finite etale and pro-etale pullbacks in this formula agree. For a tower $(N_n)$ the resulting maps to $\nu_Y^*f_{n,\mathrm{et}}^*N_n$ are compatible with its transitions, hence give
$$f^*(\varprojlim_n\nu_X^*N_n)\longrightarrow\varprojlim_n\nu_Y^*f_{n,\mathrm{et}}^*N_n.$$
This map is an isomorphism on a pulled-back trivializing covering: a compatible basis furnished by step 4 identifies it with $B_Y^r\to\varprojlim_n(A_n)_Y^r$, the coefficient-limit isomorphism coordinate by coordinate. Thus it is an isomorphism globally. This proves the inverse-limit compatibility without claiming that inverse image preserves arbitrary inverse limits.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1): pullback naturality of the residue maps and inverse-limit reconstruction

proof.text:
For a finite extension $E\subset E'$ write $A'=\mathcal O_{E'}$, choose $\varpi'$, and let $e$ be its ramification index. The scalar-extension tower of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves](3) has $m$-th term $N_{n(m)}\otimes_{A/\varpi^{n(m)}}A'/\varpi'^m$, with $n(m)=\lceil m/e\rceil$; the coefficient map exists because $\varpi^{n(m)}\in\varpi'^mA'$. Put $B'_X=\varprojlim_m(A'/\varpi'^m)_X$. With the sheaf tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], residue projections define a map
$$B'_X\otimes_{B_X}N\longrightarrow\varprojlim_m\nu_X^*\bigl(N_{n(m)}\otimes_{A/\varpi^{n(m)}}A'/\varpi'^m\bigr),$$
whose $m$-th component sends $b'\otimes x$ to $\bar b'\otimes\bar x$. The finite comparison in step 3 justifies the finite-level tensor identification. The formula commutes with transitions: both composites reduce $b'$ and $x$ to the smaller quotient. On a compatible trivializing basis for $N$ from step 4 the map is $B'_X{}^r\to\varprojlim_m(A'/\varpi'^m)_X^r$, an isomorphism by the coefficient-limit identification of step 1 applied to $E'$. Thus scalar extension corresponds to precisely this tower, and reduction and reconstruction commute with it. No flatness of a map between the finite quotient rings is used.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1) and Lemma 6.8.2: finite coefficient-extension comparisons, with the ramified reindexing of Weil II (1.1.1)

proof.text: The comparisons just constructed have the claimed normalization and coherence. On a map of modules each residue comparison commutes with that map, since both routes send $b\otimes x$ to $\bar b\otimes\overline{h(x)}$. The etale/pro-etale pullback comparisons satisfy identity and composition by [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], and inverse-image tensor comparisons do so by [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-site-inverse-image-tensor]. After those identifications, two successive module pullbacks send $c\otimes(b\otimes x)$ to $c\,f^{-1}(b)\otimes x$ along either comparison with the composite. For two coefficient extensions both composites send $c\otimes(b\otimes x)$ to $cb\otimes x$ in every residue quotient; choose a common sufficiently large source quotient when necessary. Identity maps send $1\otimes x$ to $x$. A pullback followed by coefficient extension, or the reverse, likewise sends $c\otimes(b\otimes x)$ to the same tensor with coefficient product $cb$. These formulas define maps of sheaf tensors since they respect the balancing relations and restriction maps; local pure tensors generate the sheafified tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Equalities on them give the finite-level equations. The limit comparisons satisfy the same equations because composing with each residue projection gives those equations and maps into a limit are determined by their projections.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1): identity, composition, naturality and mixed pullback/scalar-extension equations for the canonical maps

proof.text: Finally scalar localization is the sheaf tensor $N[1/\varpi]=E_X\otimes_{B_X}N$. The pullback and finite-extension comparisons extend to these rational realizations by the same balanced-tensor maps [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. On local fractions the pullback comparison sends $b\otimes(x/\varpi^k)$ to $(b\otimes x)/\varpi^k$; extension to $E'$ sends $a'\otimes(x/\varpi^k)$ to $a'\otimes x$ divided by the image of $\varpi^k$. This image is invertible in $E'$ even when the extension is ramified. These maps are isomorphisms on a pulled-back or extended finite-free basis and hence globally. On a raw rational morphism $\varpi^{-k}h$, the formula in step 6 is carried to $\varpi^{-k}f^*h$, or to the image of $\varpi^{-k}$ times the extended $h$, respectively, exactly the rational scalar-extension rule of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves](2),(3). The equations in step 9 persist on fractions, since both routes give the same coefficient product and the same integral vector. Thus rational realization commutes with the specified pullbacks and finite coefficient extensions, with the required identity and composition equations. For $X=\varnothing$ all module sheaves are zero and all formulas reduce to the unique map.
